result.title: GeoDIVE: Geospatial Descent Informed by Value Estimation
result.comment: Accepted to WACV 2027. Includes supplementary material
result.summary: Finding specific objects, structures, and spatial patterns supports critical work in agriculture, infrastructure planning, environmental monitoring, and disaster response. These features, however, are often dispersed across very large regions and span dramatically different spatial scales, which defines a search space that is costly to embed, maintain, and search naively. We introduce GeoDIVE, a model that treats a multiresolution satellite image gallery as a forest and uses best-first traversal to determine which tiles to encode. At each visited node, a lightweight model then predicts an optimistic estimate of the best query similarity hidden among its descendants using the query and subtree representations. In evaluations with image and open-vocabulary text queries, GeoDIVE matches exhaustive search at 10% of the encoding cost for image queries and leads all tested baselines at every budget in both modalities. To support future evaluation of multiscale geospatial search, we also release object-level image and text queries for Git-10M, constructed from Microsoft building footprints and OpenStreetMap polygons with VLM-generated captions. Source code and models will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: GeoDIVE 把多分辨率卫星影像库组织成树，用 best-first 遍历并由轻量模型对子树中隐藏的最优查询相似度做乐观估计，从而决定编码哪些瓦片；在图像与开放词表文本查询下以约 10% 编码成本达到穷举检索效果，并发布 Git-10M 上的多尺度检索查询。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用可学习价值估计引导分层遍历、分配编码预算的做法，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与 LOOK/计算分配提供方法线索；但对象是外部图库检索而非 VLM 内部推理状态，迁移可行性需核查。
